full_judgment:
2. The case of the petitioner, in brief, is that the case holding originally belonged to one Sk Rezvi on the basis of registered lease deed dated 26-10-62 who died in August, 1965 leaving behind wife respondent No. 4. Bahar Ara and her two minor sons Zakir Hossin Rezvi and lftekhar Rezvi. Respondent No. 4 was appointed guardian on behalf of the minor sons on 27-6-1967. Salami money of the holding was paid by 1967 and Clearance Certificate was issued on 3-5-67. Respondent No. 4 and her sons mortgaged the case holding with House Building Finance Corporation on 11-2-69, took loan and constructed building on the holding. She entered into an agreement with the petitioner to sell the properties in question and on her failure to grant sale deed the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 3 of 1979, subsequently numbered as Title Suit No. 1375 of 1981 and obtained a decree. Then the petitioner got a registered sale deed through Court on 3-1-1984. 

 3. The further case of the petitioner is that, the respondents were parties in the suit and despite the decree and sale deed through Court the property was illegally enlisted in list 'Ka' in the Gazette dated 23-6-1986 as abandoned property. 

 7. The respondent No. 2 Secretary Ministry of Works and Urban Development, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh filed an affidavit-in opposition denying the material allegations made in the Writ Petition and contending, inter alia, that the property in question has been rightly enlisted as abandoned property and the petitioner has not acquired any right on the basis of the ex parte decree which he obtained by suppression of summons and that the sale deed through Court has not conferred any title to the petitioner. 

 9. Mr Miah Abdul Gafur, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the Court of Settlement acted without lawful authority in dismissing the prayer for release of the case property and exclusion of the same from the 'Ka' list despite decree of the civil Court followed by execution and registration of sale deed in favour of the petitioner and in presence of the owner in Bangladesh all through who contested the case before the Court of Settlement and deposed before that Court supporting the sale in favour of the petitioner and acted without jurisdiction in not releasing the property since the Government failed to produce any paper in support of enlisting the case holding as abandoned property in the Gazette. He further submits that the Government is estopped from questioning the propriety of the decree and the sale deed through Court as Government was party to the suit and took several adjournments and that the property was never abandoned property within definition of the President's Order No. 16 of 1972. 

 10. Mr Md Serajul Hoque, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the respondent No. 2, however submits that the decree in question is an ex parte decree and, as such, it has no value in the eye of law. 

 13. It is found from the registered lease deed dated 26-10-62 Annexure-A to the Writ Petition that one SKB Rezvi was the original owner of the case holding. It is also found from Annexur B. Succession Certificate that Bahar Ara respondent No. 4 was appointed guardian of her two sons and the property in 1967. It is also found that respondent No. 4 mortgaged the case property with the House Building Finance Corporation as per mortgage deed, Annexur D to the petition, dated 11-2-1969. It is found from the certified copy of the order sheet of Title Suit No.3 of 1979, subsequently numbered as Title Suit No. 1375 of 1981 Annexure-F to the Writ petition, that Government was a party in that suit and took time on 14-5-79, 15-6-79 and 18-7-79 for filing written statement. Annexure-F to the Writ petition is the certified copy of the decree dated 3-9-83 which shows that respondent No.2 was the defendant No. 4 in the suit and Government of Bangladesh was defendant No. 6 in that suit which is supported by the plaint of the suit Annexure-F(1). It is found that the petitioner got his sale deed executed and registered through Court which is proved by Annexure-G to the writ petition. We find from Annexure-'K' that the vendor of the petitioner is a citizen of Bangladesh. 

 17. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner referred the case of Rahela Khatun vs. Chairman, Court of Settlement reported in 15 DLR 5 in support of his contention that the decree in question is binding on the Government who was a party in the suit and that the sale deed through Court cannot be questioned by the Government. We find that the facts of the present case and those of the case referred to above are almost similar and it fully supports the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. The learned Advocate also referred to the case of Gannysons Limited vs. Sonali Bank and others reported in 37 DLR (AD) 42 and the case of Government of Bangladesh vs. Mirza Shahab Ispahani reported in 40 DLR (AD) 116 which, in our view, support the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 

 18. The learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the respondent No.2 however referred the case of CQM Md Ayub Ali vs. Bangladesh, reported in 45 DLR 746 to show that ex parte decree is valueless. We find that the facts of that case were quite different and do not apply in this case. In this case the vendor of the petitioner never left Bangladesh rather she is admittedly a citizen of Bangladesh and admittedly sold the case land to the petitioner and she deposed before the Court of Settlement in person and also appeared in this case by filing affidavit-in-opposition and the contention of the Government that the decree was obtained by suppression of summons is belied by the order sheet of Title Suit No. 1375 of 1981.
